conventions: A string starting with "TODO:" is missing content. The site must hide it and never render the word TODO.
An empty array means no entries have been provided yet. The site must hide that block.
Stats use { value, label } so numbers can be animated; value is kept as a display string (e.g. "900k+").
projectSlugs, experience ids, research ids, competition ids and leadership ids are stable references used across sections.
The ntp-engine slug is legacy naming: the project is space nuclear POWER research, not a nuclear thermal propulsion engine.

profile.tagline: I design robots and systems for places people can't go: radioactive hot cells today, deep space next.
profile.thesis: I design robots and systems for places people can't go: radioactive hot cells today, deep space next.
about: Ana Sofía Chávez Salas is an Aerospace Engineering student at the University of Cincinnati with a minor in Materials Engineering. Her work sits at the intersection of aerospace systems, nuclear robotics, space nuclear power, and materials research.

Her engineering interests center on systems designed for extreme environments: robotic systems that operate where people cannot safely go, materials exposed to challenging conditions, and power and propulsion technologies for future space missions.
Her experiences in nuclear robotics and research led her to become increasingly interested in nuclear engineering and its applications to space exploration.

experience.summary: Developing robotic systems and path-planning methods for remote operations involving radioactive materials in environments where direct human access is not possible.
bullets: Designed a complete hot-cell layout in SolidWorks integrating four UR10 manipulators on custom actuators, extending robotic reach across a workspace inaccessible to personnel.
Designed a modular, expandable gripper system with seven grippers to date for remote handling of tools and radioactive specimens.
Prototyped grippers and components using PLA, resin, and metal.
Built a ROS2 hot-cell environment using MoveIt and RViz.
Ran 250 trials comparing five ML/AI-based path-planning methods.
Developing semi-automated path planning for four UR10 arms used in remote mechanical testing of radioactive materials.

experience.organization: Nanotechnology & Biomedicine Lab, University of Cincinnati
experience.summary: Modeling nanoparticle transport for targeted inner-ear drug delivery using multiphysics simulation.
bullets: Built COMSOL Multiphysics models of nanoparticle transport across the inner-ear membrane for targeted drug delivery.
Incorporated flow, vibration/acoustics, and electromagnetic effects into the simulation work.
Conducted parametric studies of vibration and electromagnetic factors affecting predicted delivery efficiency.

experience.summary: Provide individualized academic support to university students in STEM courses.
bullets: Tutored 50+ students in STEM courses through individualized academic support.

research.title: Component Completeness Sensitivity in Mass Optimization of Integrated Space Nuclear Power Systems
research.shortTitle: Mass Optimization of Space Nuclear Power Systems
research.context: Independent undergraduate research with faculty mentorship at the University of Cincinnati.
research.summary: Developing a modular Python thermodynamic model of an integrated nuclear reactor, closed Brayton cycle, and heat-rejection radiator to study how component-scope assumptions affect predicted mass-optimal system designs across power levels.
research.researchQuestion: How does the inclusion or omission of secondary subsystems such as radiation shielding, gas coolers, and turbomachinery mass bias the predicted mass-optimal design point of an integrated reactor–closed Brayton cycle–radiator space power system?

research.title: Multiphysics Modeling of Nanoparticle Transport for Inner-Ear Drug Delivery
research.organization: Nanotechnology & Biomedicine Lab, University of Cincinnati
research.summary: COMSOL-based multiphysics research investigating nanoparticle transport across the inner-ear membrane for targeted drug delivery.

projects.title: Robotic Hot Cell System
projects.summary: Design and development of a robotic hot-cell system for remotely handling radioactive materials in environments inaccessible to personnel.

sections.heading: Problem
body: Hot-cell environments require remote manipulation because direct human access is restricted. Robotic systems must provide sufficient reach, flexibility, and tooling to perform operations on radioactive materials.

sections.heading: Approach
body: Developed a complete SolidWorks hot-cell layout integrating four UR10 manipulators with custom actuators and designed a modular gripper architecture that allows the robots to use different tools and handle different specimens.

sections.heading: Contribution
body: Designed the hot-cell robotic layout and seven modular gripper designs and supported physical prototyping of components.

projects.title: Robotic Path-Planning Testbed
projects.summary: Simulation and evaluation of robotic path-planning approaches for semi-automated remote operations inside a nuclear hot-cell environment.

sections.heading: Problem
body: Remote nuclear operations require robots to move safely and reliably through constrained environments while reducing dependence on manual operator control.

sections.heading: Approach
body: Built a ROS2 hot-cell simulation environment using MoveIt and RViz and performed 250 trials comparing five ML/AI-based path-planning methods.

sections.heading: Contribution
body: Developed the simulation environment, performed the planning trials, and analyzed approaches toward semi-automated operation of four UR10 arms.

projects.title: Swerve Drive & Climbing System
projects.summary: Mechanical and controls development for a competition robot, including a custom swerve-drive chassis and climbing mechanism.

sections.heading: Overview
body: Designed a custom swerve-drive chassis and a SolidWorks climbing mechanism capable of lifting a 110+ lb competition robot in under 15 seconds. Developed a PID controller in LabVIEW for the robot.

projects.title: Space Nuclear Power System Mass Optimization
projects.context: Independent undergraduate research, University of Cincinnati
projects.summary: A modular computational model for investigating how subsystem completeness affects mass-optimal designs of space nuclear power systems.

sections.heading: Overview
body: The model integrates a nuclear reactor, closed Brayton-cycle power conversion system, and heat-rejection radiator. The research investigates how including or omitting secondary subsystem masses changes the predicted mass-optimal design and how that sensitivity changes with system power.

projects.title: Inner-Ear Nanoparticle Delivery Modeling
projects.organization: Nanotechnology & Biomedicine Lab, University of Cincinnati
projects.summary: Multiphysics modeling of nanoparticle transport across the inner-ear membrane for targeted drug delivery.

sections.heading: Overview
body: Built multiphysics simulations to study how flow, vibration, and electromagnetic effects influence nanoparticle transport and predicted delivery efficiency.
